title: Minesweeper Reveal
description: Reveal logic for a Minesweeper click. Hitting a mine ('M') turns to 'X'. Hitting an empty cell ('E') reveals its mine-neighbor count; if zero, flood-fill out to adjacent zero cells, stopping at numbered borders. Use a stack DFS to avoid recursion depth blow-ups on big boards.

notes: Set the cell BEFORE pushing neighbors, otherwise the same cell gets enqueued many times and you re-count its mines.
Numbered cells are flood-fill stoppers — never push their neighbors. Only zero-mine ('B') cells propagate.
Mines under the click become 'X', not 'B'. Short-circuit before entering the flood loop.

questions.q: What does the flood fill stop at?
options: Cells with at least one neighboring mine (numbered)
Any revealed cell, regardless of count

questions.q: Why mark the cell BEFORE pushing its neighbors in DFS?
options: Avoids re-processing and double-counting when the same cell is reached via multiple paths

questions.q: Clicking a numbered cell (n>0 mine-neighbors) — does the flood-fill propagate past it?
options: Yes — but only one neighbor in each direction
No — numbered cells are flood-fill stoppers; only zero-mine cells propagate
Yes — all reachable 'E' cells get revealed
No — and the cell itself stays 'E'
questions.explain: Numbered cells reveal themselves (the digit) but don't push neighbors. Only 'B' (zero-mine) cells continue the flood.

questions.q: If you initialized `let n = 1` instead of `let n = 0` before the mine-count loop, what's the bug?
options: Nothing — the count is computed correctly afterward
Every 'E' cell becomes a numbered cell (incl. zero-mine), so the flood NEVER propagates
The flood propagates correctly but cells are mis-labeled by 1
questions.explain: The `if (n > 0)` branch fires for every cell, so no cell ever takes the `else` branch that marks 'B' and pushes neighbors.

exercises.prompt: Fill in reveal so a click on a mine flips it to 'X'.

blanks.hint: mine marker after click — string literal with quotes

exercises.prompt: Fill in the flood-fill core: the numbered-stop branch condition, and the mark-before-push sentinel.

blanks.hint: numbered-cell stop condition — fires when at least one mine is adjacent
mark BEFORE pushing neighbors — same cell could be reached via many paths

L3.prompt: Implement reveal(board, click) and log JSON.stringify of the final board after clicking [3,0] on a 4x5 board with a single mine at [1,2].
hints: Short-circuit when the click hits a mine; everything else goes through the flood loop.
Count mines in the 8 neighbors; if > 0, write the digit and DO NOT recurse.
Mark blanks as 'B' BEFORE pushing their 'E' neighbors onto the stack.
